## Claims
- [proved] **Block lemma.** Let \(M\in\mathbb Z^{R\times C}\), with finite ordered sets \(C=B\sqcup D\), and let \(P\subseteq R\), \(|P|=|D|\). Put
  \[
  A=M[P,B],\qquad U=M[P,D]\in GL_{|D|}(\mathbb Z).
  \]
  If each \(r\in R\setminus P\) satisfies
  \[
  M[r,B]=M[r,D]U^{-1}A,
  \]
  then the rows indexed by \(P\) generate the complete row lattice of \(M\). The Smith diagonal of \(M\) has exactly \(|D|\) nonzero entries, all equal to \(1\), and \(\mathbb Z^C/\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Z}(M)\) is freely generated by the images of the \(B\)-coordinate vectors.

## Strategy
Write selected rows as \([A\ U]\).  For \(r\notin P\), set
\[
x_r=M[r,D]U^{-1}\in\mathbb Z^{1\times |D|},
\]
which is integral since \(U^{-1}\in\mathbb Z^{|D|\times|D|}\). The residual identity gives
\[
M[r,:]=[M[r,B]\ M[r,D]]
      =[x_rA\ x_rU]
      =x_r[A\ U].
\]
Thus every row is in the lattice generated by the selected rows; the reverse containment is immediate.

Define the unimodular column transformation
\[
W=\begin{pmatrix}
I_{|B|}&0\\
-U^{-1}A&U^{-1}
\end{pmatrix}\in GL_{|C|}(\mathbb Z).
\]
Then
\[
[A\ U]W=[0\ I_{|D|}].
\]
Every nonselected row transforms to \([0\ x_r]\), hence integral row operations subtracting \(x_r\) times the selected rows reduce \(MW\) to \([0\ I_{|D|}]\), with possible zero rows. Therefore its Smith diagonal, and hence that of \(M\), has \(|D|\) unit entries and no other nonzero entries.

For the stated original \(B\)-classes, define
\[
\pi:\mathbb Z^B\oplus\mathbb Z^D\longrightarrow\mathbb Z^B,\qquad
\pi(b,d)=b-dU^{-1}A.
\]
Its kernel is precisely
\[
\{x[A\ U]:x\in\mathbb Z^{1\times |D|}\}
=\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Z}(M).
\]
Since \(\pi(e_b)=e_b\) for each \(b\in B\), it induces an isomorphism
\[
\mathbb Z^C/\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Z}(M)\cong\mathbb Z^B,
\]
with basis given by the images of the \(B\)-coordinate vectors.

Boundary cases are included: if \(D=\varnothing\), then \(U=I_0\), the hypothesis forces all rows to vanish, and the quotient is \(\mathbb Z^B\); if \(B=\varnothing\), the quotient is \(0\).

## Gaps
This proves exactly the requested block certificate. It does not supply degreewise \((2,2,4,4)\) row/minor data or claim any parent theorem.
